keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1072-1151: the Varman land is east Bengal outside Varendra, as the pala-empire dossier draws the 1072 loss (175 cells, about 44,000 km2). The infobox 'Area' is only words: 'comprising the ancient regions of Vanga, Anga and Pundravardhana'; the text supports Vanga firmly (capital Bikrampur) and Anga and Pundravardhana only as Jatavarman's raids ('attacked Varendra', 'snatched away a part of Pundravardhana, then under the sovereign rule of Kamarupa', a struggle over Anga with the Palas), so they are not drawn. The sena-dynasty dossier's Vanga for 1152 (all of Bangladesh outside Rajshahi and Rangpur, 366 cells) is twice as large.

notes: No Cliopatria row. START: the Varman infobox says 1035 (and Jata Varman 1046-1085, Hari Varman 1085-1131); the text puts Jatavarman's rise 'in between 1050 and 1075'; the Pala page has the Varmans in east Bengal in Vigrahapala III's reign, dated 1043-1076 by five chronologies. 1072 is the pala-empire dossier's year, kept so that the two dossiers hand the land over in one year; the chandra-dynasty dossier has the Palas annexing the Chandra land in 1050, so 1050-1072 is the Palas' on the map. SUZERAINTY: the Pala page says Ramapala (reign from about 1077) 'forced the Varman king of east Bengal to accept his suzerainty' and that in Madanapala's time 'the Varmans in east Bengal declared independence'; the Varman page says Harivarman 'propitiated Ramapala in order to avoid a Pala attack'; none is dated, so no vassal_start / vassal_end is written; the pala-empire dossier should hold them with this slug as counterpart. LAND: the sena-dynasty dossier's gain for 1152 (366 cells, all Bangladesh outside Rajshahi and Rangpur) is about twice the land drawn here (175 cells, the pala-empire dossier's 1072 loss), so about 190 cells of the Sena gain have no Varman source in either dossier; the Chandra land (Comilla, Sylhet) is probably the missing part. RULERS: the infobox lists Jata Varman 1046-1085 and Hari Varman 1085-1131 and four more kings 'Unknown'; no ruler strip. DEVA: the sena-dynasty dossier's successor 'deva-dynasty' (1230) is a different dynasty from this one's predecessors.
